week.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
week.readme: AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Agents don't fit the request/response model. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent.

new.description: PyBot: a chatbot written in pure Python by a swarm of agents. No weights, no training, just rules.
new.readme: LLMs drive today’s chatbots and agents, but chatbots long predate them. Sixty years ago, ELIZA held conversations by matching patterns in what the user typed and answering with predefined templates. It could seem insightful, but its repertoire was narrow, and expanding it meant writing more rules by hand. How far could a rule-based chatbot go if a swarm of agents did that work instead?

new.description: A 4.5M-parameter two-voice English text-to-speech model, trained from scratch
new.readme: tiny-voca is a small English text-to-speech model. It has two voices, 4.5M parameters, and runs on a CPU or in the browser. Small: 4,537,291 parameters, 18 MB, waveform generator included. Fast: about 70x real time on four CPU threads. Two voices: F2 (female) and M2 (male), American English, 24 kHz. Runs anywhere: PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime Web. Open: code, weights, training recipe and dataset. Trained from scratch. Long text is fine. It is read one sentence at a time and the audio is joined.

new.description: Sculpting, animation and simulation toolkit for pixel-art Gaussian splats
new.readme: A JavaScript toolkit for sculpting signed-distance solids, baking them into pixel-art Gaussian splats, and making them move, react, break, grow and remember what happened to them. Use it from Node, drive it through the ink-studio command, or embed the source bundle in an Inkwell or browser application. The package includes geometry, materials, lighting, animation, character controls, particles, physics, procedural generation, and retained authoring.

new.description: Yab, yet another browser: a fast native macOS browser with an iPhone and Android companion
new.readme: Yet another browser. A small, quiet browser for the Mac, with an app for iPhone. Yab is a browser with nothing in the way: a row of tabs, across the top or down the left, and the page. One field takes addresses and searches. Pages run on WebKit, the engine inside every Mac, or, on Apple silicon, on Chromium, per tab or per site. Agents from the AI providers you already pay for can work in tabs of their own, and never see a private tab. One field. Type an address and you go there; type words and you search.

new.description: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
new.readme: a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics PEAR is a post-training engine for agentic robotics: it trains reasoning models to natively use robots, with reinforcement learning in simulation. PEAR is the training infrastructure behind Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots, where an open 27B reasoning model learns to use real robots entirely in simulation, with zero demonstrations.

new.description: A GTA VI PC Port
new.readme: GTA VI PC Recomp is an experimental runtime optimization framework focused on reducing shader compilation stutter, improving asset streaming responsiveness, and enhancing frame pacing consistency in Grand Theft Auto VI for PC. The project provides dynamic shader cache generation, multi-threaded asset preparation, and render pipeline optimizations designed to improve gameplay smoothness across a wide range of hardware configurations.

new.description: Run Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects unchanged on AWS, GCP, Azure or your own servers.
new.readme: Run Cloudflare Workers anywhere: AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or your own servers. The same developer experience, without the runtime limits, for a fraction of the bill. OpenOrange runs your existing Cloudflare Workers project on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure or your own servers, with no changes to your code. It's built with four goals: Zero refactoring, zero-downtime migration: your Workers and Durable Objects run as they are, and your data moves off Cloudflare while your app keeps serving.

new.description: Haru: a low-latency, multilingual, full-duplex spoken dialogue model
new.readme: Haru is a low-latency and multilingual full-duplex spoken dialogue model: it listens and speaks at the same time, the way people do on a phone call. This repository contains the inference code for Haru-4B, a pretrained base model, with three implementations and a web demo. Native full-duplex at 7.5 Hz. Every 133 ms the model takes one frame of the user's audio and produces one frame of its own audio and text.

constraints.note: Official actions with a document that make AI harder, slower or costlier to train, publish, host, reach or buy. New ones first, then those with a date still ahead or seen in the last week; every action stays in the register at data/v1/constraints.json. Magpie reports the mechanism, not the politics.

gap.method: Lag is how long before the open model's release a closed model first reached the same Capabilities Index score. Today's figure measures from that closed model to today, so it grows until an open model moves the frontier.

hardware.finding: GeForce RTX 5090 decodes fastest; DGX Spark fits the biggest models
hardware.method: Ceiling = memory bandwidth / 16 GB of weights; real decode runs below it. Fits = 80% of memory at 0.55 GB per billion parameters (4-bit). List prices are the maker's own store; street prices are dated checks of a major retailer.

possibilities.title: Consultancies under client NDAs can serve more local coding agents per DGX Spark
possibilities.why: The OpenCode LoRA lifts local Qwen3.8-27B at about one eighth the tokens, Spark Attic frees about 2 GB more KV cache on headless DGX Sparks, and DSpine speeds the same base model, so each box can carry more concurrent agent sessions.

possibilities.title: Draft models trained on base weights may lose speed on harness-tuned adapters
possibilities.why: DSpine reports 2.3x to 3.2x throughput for Qwen3.8-27B agent replays, but today's pi LoRA changes that model's outputs, so the draft model's guesses may be accepted less often.

possibilities.title: Remote Claude Code fleets in AWS get a learning loop that lowers cost
possibilities.why: Claude Code on Bedrock AgentCore runs isolated remote sessions with no cost figures, and TokenEconomizer learns from repository sessions to cut cost, so a fleet working the same repositories feeds the plugin more sessions to learn from.

possibilities.title: On-call engineers can question a whole incident's logs in a single context
possibilities.why: Headroom compresses logs and JSON before the model sees them, and Qwen4-Max holds 1 million tokens at $1.50 per million input tokens with measured lower task costs, so an entire incident window can fit cheaply.

possibilities.title: Analysts in regulated firms can query private databases with a 321B-class model on one desk
possibilities.why: The 2.48 bpw quants put a 321B-class MoE on one DGX Spark, datasette-llm can call any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and llama.cpp's new slot scheduler and prompt hashing target exactly this kind of shared local server.

viewing.title: Can Qwen 4 Max Code a 3D Renderer Without a Compiler?
viewing.why: An original hardware test, writing a 3D renderer in raw Xtensa assembly on a cheap chip, reveals Qwen 4 Max hallucinating its own screenshots while Fable succeeds.

viewing.title: 2026 in LLMs, Simon Willison, Datasette
viewing.why: Simon Willison gives a clear, first-hand account of the year's turning points, from coding agents becoming daily tools to Fable being pulled by export controls.

viewing.title: I Trapped n8n´s New AI Agent 15 Times. Did It Fall For One?
viewing.why: A careful prompt-injection test of n8n's agent, checked against server logs, shows the model held but the safety check never ran.

viewing.title: The Sentence That Makes Fable 5.2 Clean Up Your Code
viewing.why: He replicates Anthropic's ownership-sentence claim for Fable 5.2 with controlled runs. He finds it works, costs more tokens, can change behavior nobody asked for, and is cancelled by a scope rule in his setup.

viewing.title: Hugging Face Open-Sourced A Tool for Monitoring AI Agents (safeagents)
viewing.why: A live prompt injection that leaks secrets from a coding agent, then the same attack rerun with Hugging Face's safeagents proxy in the way.
